model.description: Goodwin's growth cycle with private debt added. Firms invest more when profits (net of interest on their debt) are high and less when debt is high, borrowing whatever investment their profits do not cover; wages rise only when the labour market is tight. With enough leverage, a high enough interest rate or too little debt drag, the cycle stops closing: the debt ratio ratchets up, profits are eaten by debt service, investment and employment collapse — Minsky's financial instability hypothesis as Keen (1995) first wrote it down. Watch debt_ratio: the experiment this ports flags a crisis when it passes 5.
